object_types.name: Patient
object_types.definition: A person who books and attends appointments at the clinic.

source_references.excerpt: Patients book appointments. Every appointment is booked by exactly one patient, and a patient can have many appointments... Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: PatientId
object_types.definition: A unique identifier for a patient, issued on their card.

source_references.excerpt: Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: Doctor
object_types.definition: A healthcare professional who sees patients in appointments and has a specialty.

source_references.excerpt: Each appointment is with exactly one doctor. Doctors see many patients across their appointments... Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: LicenseNumber
object_types.definition: A unique identifier for a doctor's medical license.

source_references.excerpt: Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: Appointment
object_types.definition: A scheduled meeting between a patient and a doctor at the clinic.

source_references.excerpt: Patients book appointments... Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: AppointmentNumber
object_types.definition: A unique identifier for an appointment, assigned when the appointment is created.

source_references.excerpt: Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: ExamRoom
object_types.definition: A physical room in the clinic where appointments take place.

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

object_types.name: RoomNumber
object_types.definition: A unique identifier for an exam room.

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

object_types.name: Specialty
object_types.definition: The area of medical practice in which a doctor specializes, such as cardiology or general practice.

source_references.excerpt: Every doctor has exactly one specialty, like cardiology or general practice.

object_types.name: AppointmentDate
object_types.definition: The calendar date on which an appointment is scheduled.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

object_types.name: TimeSlot
object_types.definition: A fixed time of day in which appointments can be scheduled, such as 09:00 or 09:30.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

object_types.name: AppointmentStatus
object_types.definition: The current state of an appointment.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment also has a status. The status is one of: scheduled, checked-in, completed, or cancelled. Never. An appointment always has exactly one status from that list.

object_types.name: VisitReason
object_types.definition: The reason or chief complaint provided by the patient when booking an appointment.

source_references.excerpt: An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking, and after the visit the doctor can attach a follow-up note.

object_types.name: FollowUpNote
object_types.definition: A note attached to an appointment by the doctor after the visit.

source_references.excerpt: An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking, and after the visit the doctor can attach a follow-up note. At most one follow-up note per appointment.

ambiguities.description: Scheduling uniqueness constraint unclear: Can two appointments be scheduled for the same doctor on the same date and time slot? The transcript states that appointments are booked in fixed time slots (09:00, 09:30) and that doctors see patients across appointments, but it does not explicitly state whether a doctor can have overlapping appointments or whether date+time+doctor must be unique. This affects whether the (Appointment, AppointmentDate, TimeSlot, Doctor) combination is constrained as a key.

ambiguities.description: ExamRoom participation unclear: The transcript mentions that exam rooms have a room number but does not state whether appointments are assigned to rooms or whether rooms are tracked as part of the appointment data. It is ambiguous whether the ExamRoom concept should participate in the Appointment relationship (e.g., 'Appointment takes place in ExamRoom') or whether rooms are managed separately.

ambiguities.description: Temporal state of primary doctor: The transcript states 'every patient has exactly one primary doctor' but does not clarify whether this is a current-state relationship or a historical one. It is unclear whether a patient's primary doctor can change over time and whether history should be tracked.

ambiguities.description: Status transitions: The transcript lists the allowed appointment status values (scheduled, checked-in, completed, cancelled) but does not specify valid state transitions. For instance, it is unclear whether a cancelled appointment can transition to completed, or whether there are prerequisite states (e.g., must be scheduled before checked-in).
